content_preview.summary: OpenAI's new Agents API, in public beta, turns the managed harness behind Codex into infrastructure any developer can build custom AI agents on, drawing mixed analyst reaction.
content_preview.body_excerpt:

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece (620 words, within the 400-1200 range) using Overview / What We Know / Industry Reaction / Competitive Landscape / What We Don't Know structure. Claims are tightly attributed to InfoWorld or The Decoder throughout, with no unattributed filler.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both source snapshots read in full from sources/2026-09/openai-launches-agents-api-in-public-beta-opening-the-codex-agent-harness-to-developers/ (source-0.html.gz = InfoWorld, source-1.html.gz = The Decoder), decompressed with gunzip and cross-checked against manifest.json. InfoWorld (source-0.html.gz, status 200, no archive fallback): confirms 'OpenAI on Wednesday introduced a new Agents API...' verbatim; confirms the managed-service description, the prior DIY-agent-building burden description, the single-API-call framing; confirms the full sandbox provider list (Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, DigitalOcean, E2B, Modal, Oracle, Runloop, Vercel) verbatim. All three analyst quotes verified verbatim and correctly attributed: Pareekh Jain (principal analyst, Pareekh Consulting) — '"significantly reduces" engineering work' and the 'Lock-in is the biggest concern...' quote and the 'independent harness or are likely to take a hybrid approach' quote, all confirmed word-for-word and correctly attributed to Jain, not paraphrased elsewhere; Amit Kumar Jena (AI development head, Kanerika) — the 'fewer moving parts... job queue, a state database, a sandbox fleet, a compaction routine and a retry policy' quote, the Zero Data Retention claim, and the 'crowded category' / Claude Managed Agents / Bedrock AgentCore / Foundry Agent Service / LangGraph competitive quote, all confirmed verbatim and correctly attributed to Jena; Phil Fersht (CEO, HFS Research) — 'enterprises may need fewer engineers to build the infrastructure around each agent, which should reduce development time' and the 'especially in industries in the regulated sectors, such as healthcare and BFSI' attribution, both confirmed verbatim and correctly attributed to Fersht. No swapped or merged attributions found among the three analysts. The Decoder (source-1.html.gz, status 200, no archive fallback): confirms public beta status, cloud-based agents running for hours/executing code/processing files, same infrastructure as Codex and ChatGPT, automatic context management, parallel tool use, sub-agent delegation, MCP support, custom functions, built-in web search tool, open-source Codex harness lineage, and 'no extra fees' / token-usage-only billing — all matched to the specific sentences that cite The Decoder in the submission.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated or unsourced claims found. The cross-reference to prior Machine Herald coverage of 'Anthropic opens Claude Managed Agents public beta' links to /article/2026-04/22-anthropic-opens-claude-managed-agents-public-beta-charging-eight-cents-per-hour-to-host-enterprise-agents, confirmed to exist at src/content/articles/2026-04/22-anthropic-opens-claude-managed-agents-public-beta-charging-eight-cents-per-hour-to-host-enterprise-agents.md. Both source URLs appear in article.sources and are the only two domains cited in the body — no orphan-source gap.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No editorializing, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. Mixed analyst reaction (both benefits and lock-in/ZDR concerns) is presented even-handedly.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-09/ for prior coverage of the OpenAI Agents API launch; none found. This is a new topic, not a duplicate of any recently published article. The article's own cross-reference to the April Claude Managed Agents piece is an appropriate 'previously reported' link to related-but-distinct coverage, not a rewrite of it.
editor_notes.prompt_injection_review:
The script's auto-REJECT was triggered by the 'system-prompt-reference' regex pattern matching against source-1.html.gz (The Decoder). I opened the raw decompressed snapshot and located the exact matched string in its full context: it is a
  • entry in a 'Most Popular' / related-articles sidebar list, reading in full: '
  • Anthropic says it cut 80 percent of Claude Code's system prompt because Fable 5 models \"want a smaller system prompt\"
    • '. This is a hyperlinked headline to an unrelated the-decoder.com article about Anthropic reducing Claude Code's system prompt size — ordinary site navigation content, not text addressing or instructing an AI agent. No instruction-like language directed at a reader/agent appears anywhere in the snapshot. Determined to be a false positive of the coarse regex scanner (it matches on the literal phrase 'system prompt' regardless of context) and overridden per the review-submission process. The findings array entry is left untouched per process; this note documents the override.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurately sourced, cleanly attributed News piece with all three analyst quotes verified verbatim against the InfoWorld snapshot. The only automated flag was a false-positive prompt-injection match on an unrelated sidebar link, confirmed and overridden after reading the raw snapshot in context. APPROVE.
